lines.en: And so she did...
Just not really.
You see, making friends is way harder than it seems when you’re observing the inner and outer circles of a bunch of girls who, for the most part, need companionship in order to survive.
But, at the same time, if you’re one of those mythical “extroverts,” you’re probably reading this right now and thinking to yourself, “Well, it’s never been that hard for me!”
And the reason for that is simple — you live in the moment. But you live in a way that disallows you to see more than five minutes into the future. And hey, maybe that’s okay for you.
Maybe that makes you happy.
After all, when the opposing side’s world-view is more typically synonymous with staring so far into the future that they lose sight of the present altogether, extroversion sounds pretty tempting.

None of this is to say those personality types are confined to this alone, though. There’s a lot more that goes into both of them, I’m sure. And this is just one person’s paraphrased interpretation of them.
I guess all I’m saying is that just because some things are easy for some people doesn’t mean that it’s like that for everyone.
If you want to see that as weakness, fine. I know doing that makes me feel a little better about myself sometimes, so it’s not like I’ll blame you or anything if that’s the path you want to take.
I just want to urge you to maybe think outside of the box sometimes since what’s inside might not be all it's cracked up to be.
Regardless, in the white-haired girl’s half-desperate plea for someone to listen to her, things begin to bubble up.
Some of the others wonder if it’s worth it. Some have already made up their minds. Some might even already see her as a friend.
But that’s not the way that girl sees anyone. Even Touka, the one who has essentially become a stand-in mother figure for Yasu, was not exactly a “friend” in her somewhat-seeing eyes.
She was more like a shadow. Something both real and not real at the same time. An entity that, while taking up visual space, was naught more than a distortion in the grand scheme of things.
But what is that scheme, you ask?
And it’s a good question.
: Okay, everyone! It’s time for the next competition!
But it’s one that won’t be answered until later.
I’m sure you’ve probably already come to expect that, though.
Answers never come easy around here, do they?
And besides, even when your questions are answered, you like to pretend they’re not because the idea of closure is kind of intimidating. It’s a little bit scary.
But it’s nothing like living in a world where you constantly lose sight of the present.
I hope, from the bottom of my heart-
That you never have to deal with those bubbles.
: First and foremost, I’d like to ask all of our viewers at home to kindly forget anything they may have heard when I was talking to my friends a few minutes ago.
: I can assure you that I am perfectly sane. But since assuring you of my sanity probably makes me sound insane instead, forget I said that too!
: Miss Imai...the scavenger hunt?
: Right!
: With the current contest tied at two points apiece, this next one, a sports day classic, will determine who heads into the second half of the day with an advantage!
: And while that advantage could be thrown out of the window at any moment, it’ll definitely add to the weight of things given that there are now two absent members of the first floor.
: This “one point deduction for everyone who doesn’t participate” thing is pretty rough, huh? Extra work while getting slapped with that can’t be a fun combination.
: It’s not...but I understand the reasoning for it. Sports day is all about working as a team and, if there are any weak links, it only makes sense that everyone has to pay for it.
: Exactly! Just don’t let those words get in the way of the fact that the scavenger hunt is going to be an individual competition and doesn’t have much to do with teamwork at all!
: It kind of vaguely does in the sense that we had to elect who’d be participating, right?
: Sure! But anything can mean anything so long as you’re really vague about it.
: Just look at the entire existence of modern art. We live in a world where you can accidentally spill your coffee on a canvas and then sell it for millions of dollars in the right setting.
: Is this really the time and place to be having a discussion on modern art?
: No! Which is why I will now explain the rules of the competition for anyone at home who needs a quick refresher!
: Just behind us, you’ll find a bunch of note cards scattered all over the ground.
: Each one of these note cards has something you’ll need to find written on the back, and they were all written based on suggestions from our viewers.
: And while that was fun and all, it also taught me that there are some really creepy people who watch our show! So please note that these have been heavily censored.
: Heavily censored. You’re welcome.
: Maybe we should stop televising this event?
: Maybe! But anyway, all you two need to do is overturn those cards one at a time, collect the object on the card, and bring it back to the center circle to gain a point!
: The contest will immediately come to an end after one of you reaches three points, but beware! For there are some things on these cards that will be very hard to find!
: Can we just...get a new card if the object on the one we overturn looks too hard?
: Nope! You’ve just gotta chalk it up to bad luck and deal with it. That’s life, girls.
: So when do we-
: Ah!
: Ah!
: Ah!
: Sorry, Miku! Go, Futaba! Go, Otoha! Fight to the death in heavily-censored fashion!
: Um...Otoha?
: Hey.
: What are you doing?
: Preventing you from flipping over this card.
: Oh...okay.
: Why?
: Because I figure that if I can wear you down and just prevent you from picking up any cards to begin with that I’ll be able to outlast you and ultimately win. It’s nothing personal.
: So you just...won’t pick up any cards yourself until...I’m tired?
: That’s the plan.
: And...if I don’t get tired? Then what?
: I don’t know.
: It’s not a well thought out plan. I just saw you reaching for this one and reacted instinctively.
: Why is your first instinct to sabotage me?!
: I don’t know, Futaba! I’ve been learning a lot of things about myself lately and I don’t like any of them! Just chalk this up to another character flaw and find another card!
: But I want this one!
: There are like fifty fucking cards on the ground! Just pick any of them! It doesn’t matter!
: You heard her! Let go!
: I can’t! It’s a matter of principle at this point!
: Aaaahhhh fine! Take your stupid card! I’ll take this one instead!
: Ha! You shouldn’t have let go so easily, Otoha! Because now, all I have to find is- oh. What? Why?
: Ha! It was a diversionary tactic all along! Good luck, Futaba! You’ve fallen for my trap!
: Don’t pretend that you did this on purpose, Otoha! I know your games!
: She won’t rest until she’s destroyed our entire dorm, Futaba! Don’t let it get to you!
: What kinda stuff do ya think our viewers are makin’ the girls look for?
: I’m not sure. But I do know that Imani asked to borrow some money from me so she could buy supplies. I think Touka wound up covering it, though.
: Is that...what all of those crates are for?
: I know my mom donated at least one box worth of supplies this year. I have no idea what they were for, though.
: Yeah, I think I might know.
: You okay, Rin? You look nervous.
: My best friend and my ex are competing in a fight to the death right now. Of course I’m nervous.
: I don’t...think it’s...to the death, Rin...
: Until one of them flips over a card that says “murder” and they’re forced to do something they’d probably never do under normal circumstances.
: And I only say “probably” because you never know when someone is going to turn out to be a serial killer and I can never rule out that possibility for anyone.
: Correct me if I’m wrong...but don’t you, like...collect skulls and shit? Wouldn’t that make you the prime suspect for something like that?
: Only as decorations! If Euronymous from Mayhem can make necklaces out of his bandmate’s skull then surely I can put a few unidentified ones on my shelf without evoking suspicion, can’t I?
: I’d make a bone necklace. That sounds kind of fun.
: I feel like...there have been a lot of references...most people won’t understand lately...
: Done! Imani, look!
: M-Me too!
: But why a sword?...
: Otoha! You were first! What was written on your card?
: Please tell me it was something flattering and not “annoying Irish girl whose screen-time has really tapered off lately.”
: Something white!
: There had to have been easier alternatives than me!
: There were. But I figured you might enjoy being princess carried and thought I had some spare time since Futaba seemed worried about her card.
: I think I love you.
: Don’t even think about it, Molly!
: Futaba! What did your card say?
: Sword?
: Points awarded to both of you! The score is even at one point each! Now go get your new cards and-
: Fuck! Where the hell am I going to get one of these?!
: Otoha! Did you really have to drop me?! Has my love been that poorly received again?!
: Oh! This should be much easier! Thank you, mystery viewer!
: Go, Futaba! Go! Just two more points left!
: Fuck her up, Otoha! Just not in a violent or mean way because Futaba is our precious cupcake and hurting her is cause for exile!
: She’s much more than just a “cupcake,” Noriko. She’s a sunlit cobweb in the corner of your grandmother’s cottage that you look to for comfort following her passing.
: She’s got nice tits.
: That too.
: Guys, where is Otoha going?
: I think I have an idea, but I don’t want to spoil the surprise.
: I have returned! And with a slightly hotter body temperature!
: We called that “the Otoha Effect” at our old school. Only a handful of us were immune.
: It appears that you have been charmed, Emerald Guardian. Perhaps your normal status will be recovered after our next short rest?
: One can not simply get rid of the Otoha Effect. It’s a thing you must live with from that point on.
: I still have dreams about her sometimes. But I have accepted that some things can simply never be.
: If I may ask, what exactly about Otoha makes her as appealing as she apparently is to other girls? Because, despite never talking to her at our previous school, I never mistook her for a male.
: I don’t think any of us mistook her for a male. Most of us are just also attracted to girls.
: Is bisexuality really that common in today’s society?
: Are you not at all interested in girls, Touka? Like...not even a little?
: I can admire beauty when I see it. For example, I think Tsuneyo is extraordinarily attractive.
: Thanks, bro.
: You’re welcome, bro. But I am not attracted to her. Are all of you saying that you are?
: Yeah.
: Absolutely.
: Oh yeah.
: God yes.
: Affirmative.
: Interesting.
: Being the most desirable cast member is such a burden sometimes.
: Otoha, what the fuck?!
: It appears that my largest contribution to this event has been discovered.
: Get out of the way!
: Where did you get that?!
: I found it!
: Where?!
: I just did, okay?! Now, get out of the frickin’ way before I kill you! I’m not certified to drive this thing!
: Futaba! What was on your card?!
: Flowers!
: Otoha!
: Forklift!
: Imani, I’ve been gone for ten minutes.
: How have you managed to create such a disturbance within that minuscule timeframe?
: You call it a disturbance. I call it awesome.
: I’ll be damned. Your lack of sexual contact has transitioned into such a deep state of hysteria that I can’t help but feel like I should take care of you myself.
: Lucky for you, I’ve already come up with a gameplan on how we can convince Osako! First, you have to blindfold her. Then-
: Imani, I was kidding.
: Yeah.
: Me too.
: I am so lonely.
: Miss Imai!
: Huh? What?
: I need to steal you for a second.
: Fucking forklift! If I didn’t have to park it, I’d already have my third card by now too!
: This for the scavenger hunt?
: Is that not obvious?
: It is. But, fair warning — I don’t care how precious and lovable you are. If that card says “something black,” I ain’t afraid to slap a bitch.
: It’s not “something black.” Just...
: Come with me...
: Uhh...okay, viewers! It looks like the final object in Futaba’s scavenger hunt is somehow me!
: Which means it looks like I have lost.
: Not yet, Otoha! Futaba needs to reveal her card before we can find out whether or not I even relate to it and-
: My final card is “something beautiful.” And it was the easiest one of all because the most beautiful woman I know has been right here all along.
: I don’t want to ruin the moment because Imani is definitely beautiful, but saying it was the easiest one when we also had cards like “sword” and “forklift” isn’t really doing much.
: That’s true. I’ve never been great at giving speeches, so having to do this in front of millions of live viewers is somewhat daunting, but...
: If Miss Imai can hear how all of us feel about her, I think that would make everyone really happy.
: No objections from me. Because, even though I lost the competition, I got to drive a forklift. Which means I'm the real winner when all is said and done.
: Uhh...
: I mean...
: I guess...that might count...maybe...
: It counts, Imani. All of us are well aware of how hot you are.
: It’s hard to ignore it, to be honest. It’s almost distracting sometimes.
: Sometimes? We’ve got two of the most attractive teachers in the whole damn world. That’s why all of our grades are bad. It’s not just us.
: It’s not “just you” in the first place. Only a handful of you have bad grades. The rest of us are actually near the top of the school.
: Shh! We’re talking about how cute Imani is right now! Grade stuff can wait!
: Imani! We love you and you make us feel things!
: Hey! How come I get in trouble whenever I say stuff like that but you can all do it whenever you want?!
: Context is important, Kirin. And I say this as someone who routinely sodomizes it.
: Nodoka’s right. Like, a scavenger hunt card that says “something beautiful?” Cool. Just telling her you want to fuck her in the middle of math? Not cool.
: I can’t help when the feelings arise, Noriko! I’ve been fucking affection starved lately and I’m going through withdrawal!
: Curious. I wonder what sort of developments there have been lately that could have led to a decrease of affection aimed toward Kirin?
: It doesn’t matter what developments there have been, Makoto! What matters is that you should all say nice things about me now since Imani’s already gotten her five minutes of fame.
: K-Kirin’s right! Go...say nice things about her or whatever. Futaba wins the...scavenger thing and...I’m gonna...I’m gonna see what I can do about this forklift.
And so we pass the half-way point of the Super Mega Ultimate Sports-Day Dorm Wars: No Boys Allowed! The Extremely Awesome and Only Kind of Sad Special Event for Bonding and Battling!
